name: Sebirwa
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Zsiga, Elizabeth. 2018. In favor of [fortis]: evidence from Setswana and Sebirwa. Proceedings of the Annual Meetings on Phonology 5 (AMP 2017). Washington, DC: Linguistic Society of America. doi:10.3765/amp.v5i0.4252 (open LSA proceedings PDF, 12 pp.)
catalog_locator: p.8, section 5 'Comparison to Sebirwa: In favor of [voice]' (Sebirwa statement); p.3, section 2 'The problem of Setswana' (the Setswana reference statement); p.6, section 3 (phrase-final weakening); p.5, section 3 'Setswana data and analysis' (production experiment).
catalog_quote: [p.8] Setswana and Sebirwa are both Sotho-Tswana languages spoken in Botswana. [...] Sebirwa, in contrast, is not recognized as an official language and is not written. It is spoken by a small ethnic minority in the far eastern corner of Botswana (adjacent to the Sengwato dialect area). The phonetic data presented here (summarizing data reported in Zsiga and Boyer 2017) is based on fieldwork conducted in the village of Molalatau. [...] The one previous phonological description of Sebirwa in the literature is Chebanne (2000), which consists of a tentative inventory, historical notes, and a short phonological description based on phonetic data elicited from ten speakers, all older than 75 years. [...] Sebirwa has the same syllable structure and stress pattern as Setswana, and many words are cognate. [p.3, on Setswana:] The only syllable types allowed are CV, V, or a syllabic nasal, and stress is consistently penultimate.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Sebirwa falls on the penultimate syllable, as in Setswana (syllables are CV, V or syllabic nasal); stated by equating Sebirwa's stress pattern with Setswana's, which the same paper describes as consistently penultimate.
new_statements.exceptions: None. The paper notes phrase-final syllables are unstressed and weakened (for Setswana), nothing Sebirwa-specific.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated as a general word-level pattern; data are words in citation and short carrier utterances from nine to ten elderly speakers in Molalatau, Botswana. The Sebirwa statement is indirect (by reference to Setswana) and brief; no dedicated prosody section exists in any accessible Sebirwa description.
new_statements.identity_note: Zsiga 2018 and Zsiga & Boyer describe Sebirwa as spoken in Molalatau village, Bobonong sub-district, eastern Botswana (fieldwork with nine to ten elderly speakers); Chebanne 2000 also Bobonong sub-district. The Zimbabwean variety (called 'Sotho' of Gwanda) and South African Birwa are not covered. All fall under birw1238.
